![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228292/assets/5484647a9c694b95bd9e4b569c84f7263c5e69de5e98f12a1081fd937d298769.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $KMLK,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={C}_{1}\cup \{-{C}_{2}\}\cup \{-{C}_{3}\},
$$

where $-{C}_{2}$ and $-{C}_{3}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$
